pr_title: Add original filename column to file table on Windows
pr_body:
Add original filename column to file table on Windows as requested in #7115 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/33552046/121736176-81e60380-caf7-11eb-8e44-420f89dca346.png)
pr_comments:
The committers are authorized under a signed CLA.
  • :white_check_mark: fneur (169315798115a7f290531a560f705755eb590526)
@theopolis Can you re-run the checks, please? After merging #7148 those problems in *build_windows* should be gone? (#7148 had exactly the same problems before the final code changes)

I like the feature/PR! But one question I have is, the `original filename` only exists on some PE files correct? I dont think it exists on any other file type (ex: txt, py, etc)?
Would this be better under a dedicated PE table?
I think `original filename, product_version, and file version` all only exist on some PE files?
Although since `product_version and file version` already exist on `file` it could be nice to include `original filename` too.
Again, i like the feature and it would cool to add something like this either under the `file` table or a dedicated PE table (or both).

@puffyCid Thanks for your comment! You are right. According to [Microsoft](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/menurc/about-version-information),

> you can add version information to any files that can have Windows resources,
> such as DLLs, executable files, or .fon font files. 

This applies to all three properties: `original_filename`, `product_version` and `file_version`.

> Would this be better under a dedicated PE table?

This would certainly make sense as the resource section (containing the version information) is just one of many sections inside a PE file. From a usability perspective, though, I'd favour the addition to the file table.
How to proceed with this PR?

I think we should consider breaking out the PE-specific attributes into a dedicated table, but until then we can continue the precedent we have of using the windows-specific schema and add this as another column.

If @farfella is OK from a code+implementation review then we can merge.

> I think we should consider breaking out the PE-specific attributes into a dedicated table, but until then we can continue the precedent we have of using the windows-specific schema and add this as another column.

Sorry, just a small shameless plug, but the PR at #7160 adds a dedicated PE table that shows `original filename, product_version, and file version` and a bit more.  
This PR was open shortly before mine was, the overlap between the two was accidental (The main focus of my PR was to close #7054, which also closes a several others issues as a result due the features it adds).  As i mentioned in my first comment i appreciate the work put in this PR, maybe both implementations can exist?

It looks like this PR is ready to be merged soon, while the one i opened (#7160) still needs to be reviewed. Perhaps this could be merged and then updated again when #7160 is merged?
Again it wasnt my intention to overlap with this PR with my own, sorry.
Good to go. Sorry for the delay. I need 36-hour days. :)
How to proceed with this PR?

I just built and tested this on Windows 11, works as described. LGTM

But since the `original_filename` property only belongs to PE format files, as has been discussed already, shouldn't we clarify this in the table spec? Just with a little comment like `Column("original_filename", TEXT, "(Executable files only) Original filename"),`
Many thanks to everyone involved in bringing this PR forward. Cheers, F.

review_comments: Could doing this for every call to platformStat impact performance? It may be more performant to have a seperate method to query this information, as even though you might need to open the file handle a second time you could adjust the file table to only call this if the original_filename column is used.

It's hard to say. Taking a cursory look at `platformStat` I think it may have some issues. For example, I see it calling `CloseHandle` on an `INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE`.  I suspect the implementation of `platformStat` itself could be optimized.

Complexity-wise I think this function is similar to the `windowsGetVersionInfo` function, which is called by `platformStat` just above the call to `windowsGetOriginalFilename` (and unconditionally so). What's more, the sequence of Windows API calls carried out by these functions is similar, too. (Also note that the `for` loops will be trivial in the typical case, with loop iterations <= 1) . So, performance-related issues are not expected. Do you see any specific problems I might have overlooked?

One last thing:
Due to their similar nature, `windowsGetVersionInfo` and `windowsGetOriginalFilename` could be combined into a single function to avoid certain redundancies.
Sounds good to me, I don't see any other problems.
